title: fix: honor ID member agent policy for new sessions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ID members being able to create a session for an agent excluded by their membership role when linked to a local profile with broader permissions. The same creation policy also applies when resetting a session that does not exist yet.

## User Impact

New sessions honor the member’s agent policy. Existing-session access, local profile permissions, owner access, and reset’s admin-scope requirement keep their current behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the operator authority already retained by the session owner for creation checks, including catalog imports, instead of falling back to the linked profile’s role. This adds no new identity channel or state.

## Evidence

- All four new create/reset regressions failed on the base and pass on `1a6acc7ed5d2`. Supporting role, creation, reset/fork, recovery, and catalog-import tests passed across seven files.
- Final commit: core and both affected test TypeScript checks, type-aware lint/format for all seven files, and `pnpm build:runtime` passed.
- Isolated compiled-Gateway replay passed using a real local issuer, Discovery, and native iroh transport. Write-only creation and separately admin-scoped reset both reject excluded agents without persisting a row; explicit agent grants, linked local-admin operations, existing-session operations, and owner operations succeed. Write-only reset remains refused by its existing scope gate. This is isolated source-checkout qualification, not deployed-service validation.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. Codex API autoreview covered the complete seven-file repair snapshot through P3 with no actionable findings; independent source review also covered the final type-only correction. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43674662662), and [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199413#issuecomment-6889046169) found no actionable findings or before-merge items. The hosted reviewer could inspect source and CI; the native runtime trace remains in the private validation evidence.
